sections.skill: Recognize affirming the consequent and denying the antecedent

questions.prompt: "If a phone is waterproof, it survives a fall into a pool. Leo's phone survived a fall into a pool. So Leo's phone is waterproof." What is wrong with this argument?

choices.text: It affirms the consequent: the phone may have survived for another reason.

questions.correct_answer: It affirms the consequent: the phone may have survived for another reason.

questions.prompt: "If n is a multiple of 4, then n is even. 6 is not a multiple of 4. So 6 is not even." What is wrong?

choices.text: It denies the antecedent: not P does not give not Q.

questions.correct_answer: It denies the antecedent: not P does not give not Q.

questions.prompt: This form is valid: "If P then Q. Q. So P."
Use whole numbers to show that "If n is a multiple of 6, then n is even. n is even. So n is a multiple of 6." is invalid: give a value of n that makes both premises true and the conclusion false.
questions.rule: (isEven(n) and n % 6 != 0) and isInteger(n) and n >= 0
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: (isEven(n) and n % 6 != 0) and isInteger(n) and n >= 0 (example: n = 4)

questions.prompt: Which argument is VALID?

choices.text: "If it rains, the game is off. The game is off. So it is raining."
"If it rains, the game is off. It is not raining. So the game is not off."
"If it rains, the game is off. So if the game is off, it rains."
"If it rains, the game is off. The game is not off. So it is not raining."

questions.correct_answer: "If it rains, the game is off. The game is not off. So it is not raining."

sections.relationship: Invalid forms are recognized by comparing them with the valid forms they imitate.
sections.author_note: Invalid forms are recognized by comparing them with the valid forms they imitate.

questions.prompt: "If P then Q. P. So Q." What is this form called?
"If P then Q. Not Q. So not P." What is this form called?
Modus ponens is valid.
Modus tollens is valid.
In modus ponens, which part of the conditional is given as a fact?

sections.relationship: Students see that an invalid form "feels" right; a case with true premises and a false conclusion proves it is invalid.
sections.author_note: Students see that an invalid form "feels" right; a case with true premises and a false conclusion proves it is invalid.

questions.prompt: An argument form is invalid if there is one case with all premises true and the conclusion false.
"If x > 5, then x > 2. x > 2. So x > 5." Which value of x shows it is invalid?
A valid argument can have true premises and a false conclusion.
"If an animal is a robin, it has wings. A bat has wings. So a bat is a robin." Which fact shows the form is invalid?

choices.text: A bat has wings but is not a robin.

questions.correct_answer: A bat has wings but is not a robin.

questions.prompt: If one case with true premises has a true conclusion, the argument is valid.

sections.relationship: Harder: invalid forms in everyday wording and with "only if".
sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: "The alarm sounds only if there is smoke. There is smoke. So the alarm sounds." Is this valid?

choices.text: No: "A only if S" means "if A then S"; from S, A does not follow.
Yes: smoke always sets off alarms.

questions.correct_answer: No: "A only if S" means "if A then S"; from S, A does not follow.

questions.prompt: "Every square is a rectangle. This shape is not a square. So it is not a rectangle." This argument is valid.
Show that "If x > 10, then x > 3. x is not greater than 10. So x is not greater than 3." is invalid: give a number x that makes the premises true and the conclusion false.
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: not (x > 10) and x > 3 (example: x = 5)

questions.prompt: Which argument has the SAME form as "If it is a cat, it is a mammal. It is a mammal. So it is a cat."?

choices.text: "If n is 2, n is even. n is even. So n is 2."
"n is 2 or n is 3. n is not 3. So n is 2."
"If n is 2, n is even. n is 2. So n is even."
"If n is 2, n is even. n is odd. So n is not 2."

questions.correct_answer: "If n is 2, n is even. n is even. So n is 2."

questions.prompt: Denying the antecedent and affirming the consequent are both invalid.

sections.relationship: Expert: separate an invalid form from an argument with true premises and conclusion.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: "If a number is divisible by 4, it is even. 12 is even. So 12 is divisible by 4." The conclusion is true, so the argument is valid.

For whole numbers n from 1 to 30, the argument "If n is a multiple of 6, then n is even. n is even. So n is a multiple of 6." has true premises for every even n. For how many of these n is the conclusion false?
Which argument is INVALID, even though every premise and the conclusion are true?

choices.text: "If 9 is even, then 9 is a whole number. 9 is even. So 9 is a whole number."
"9 is odd or 9 is even. 9 is not even. So 9 is odd."
"If 9 is odd, then 9 is a whole number. 9 is a whole number. So 9 is odd."
"If 9 is odd, then 9 is a whole number. 9 is odd. So 9 is a whole number."

questions.correct_answer: "If 9 is odd, then 9 is a whole number. 9 is a whole number. So 9 is odd."

questions.prompt: Valid: "If P then Q. If not P then Q. So Q."
Valid: "If P then Q. If Q then P. Not P. So not Q."
